checks.statement_fidelity: pass for the local lemmas, under readings that are reported and carry questions. (i) Lemma 2.6(i), lem_curve_extension_i. It gives: the rim value tau^R; positivity on the closed disc 0 <= r <= R; global continuity; two pieces (the slice M/R on r <= R/2 and a C^n piece on r >= R/2, each IsSpacelikeGraph); the graph spacelike over the closed disc in the integrated form IsSpacelikeDiscGraph; and IsCompact (discGraphSet). The printed construction (l.872-877, under the swapped label) is the one used. min(M/R, piece) = tau on 0 < r <= R and delta >= 1 are proved, not assumed. IsSpacelikeDiscGraph is a non-trivial notion: it requires strict increase of the height along E0's Le between distinct points with rad <= R, axis included. It is inhabited by 2.6(i)'s disc. As a conclusion it is weaker than a pointwise 'spacelike at the axis', which has no derivative meaning at the axis. Disclosed with a question. (ii) Lemma 2.9, lem_intersect_number_compact. The hypotheses are weaker than the paper's: J^+(p) is dropped, and c only needs to be continuous and Le-monotone on an OrdConnected I with rad <= R. The K-3 end conditions (a point strictly below Sigma; tau unbounded or a last point on the shaft) follow from 'closed in S, inextendible in Int S'. r and tau are non-decreasing along Le (rad_le_of_le, fst_le_of_le), so a curve ending at rad y <= R stays in the cylinder. The count matches the paper's: ncard = if sup in J^+(C) or +infinity then 1 else 0. Non-vacuity: the axis ray (lem_intersect_number_compact_axis). (iii) Cor 2.11, cor_intersect_number. The hypotheses are 2.9's for c and 2.10's (K-3) for c* = c restricted to I* = {t | rad(c t) > 0}, with C = C* read as gc = gs on r = R. I checked that hpast' cannot be dropped. It forces I* to be non-empty: a curve lying entirely on the axis meets Sigma once and Sigma* zero times. It also covers the case of a curve starting between Sigma* and Sigma. Both cases violate the paper's 'inf(c) in the head', so assuming both lemmas' K-3 past conditions is the faithful reading of 'under the hypotheses of Lemmas 2.9 and 2.10'. The proof transfers sup-conditions correctly: I* is a final segment, a last point on the shaft lies in I*, and the rim sets agree. The joint hypotheses are inhabited (cor_intersect_number_vertical, with 2.6(i)'s disc and 2.6(ii)'s cusp on the same rim). (iv) Lemmas 2.6(ii), 2.7, 2.8 and 2.10 and spear_surgery_local are unchanged from WP-41j, which AUDIT-2 of that package found clean, and I re-read the statements. (v) regM_isCauchyComplete: hCC is a topological compact Cauchy surface. That is weaker than B21 l.227's smooth spacelike one, so the statement is stronger than the paper's. This is allowed and disclosed, and it is consistent with the project's E0CauchyCompact (AbsMax.lean l.671), which is topological and acausal and so implies hCC. Its consumer AbsMax.lean l.997 can therefore call it.

issues.problem: The dispatch's first item, 'the global part of the surgery (its tagged sorry)', was not attempted. WP-43b adds no declaration toward it: no construction of Sigma*, no per-spear gluing lemma, no statement of the Remark 2.12 curve lemma, no completeness-gluing lemma. Only the SORRY text was rewritten. AUDIT-1 M3 of WP-41j asked for this decomposition, and AUDIT-2 m4 asked again. Of the three 'GENUINE obstructions' named, (2) CURVES ('relative curve-extension theory ... absent') and (3) LENGTH ('edist comparison on chart domains and path lifting strip -> Sigma* cap spear are not in the library') are unbuilt infrastructure, not mathematical obstructions. The campaign protocol and DEC-23 ask that they be built, or at least isolated. Obstruction (1) REGULARITY is genuine only relative to the topological reading of hCC. The REPORT notes itself say it disappears under B21 l.227's smooth reading, and the paper-faithful variant AUDIT-2 m4 suggested (a smooth or C^1 spacelike compact Cauchy surface, or a C^1 rim datum) was not stated. Mitigation: the theorem cannot be sorry-free this round in any case. It rests on GXScaffold.BTZ.Spear's tagged sorries (globallyHyperbolic_glued l.2301, isCauchySurface_glued l.2311, the future case of lem_add_BTZ_param_line l.3211), all three confirmed present. The row is honestly reported as 'stated', so this is not a blocker.
